summary: The BMW 3 Series (E46) is the fourth generation of BMW's 3 Series compact executive cars, made from 1997 to 2006. It replaced the E36 and was sold in five body styles, including a hatchback marketed as the 3 Series Compact. BMW said its body was 70% more rigid than the E36's. It kept rear-wheel drive and a 50/50 weight distribution, and brought back all-wheel drive on some models. It was the first 3 Series offered with a Valvetronic engine, and it introduced features such as satellite navigation and rain-sensing wipers to the range. The M3 performance model arrived in 2000 with a straight-six engine. Sales peaked in 2002. The E90 began replacing it in late 2004, and the last coupés and convertibles were built in 2006. Andy Priaulx won the 2004 European and 2005 World Touring Car titles in an E46 320i.
